summary: S. 389 requires the Consumer Product Safety Commission to issue a final consumer product safety rule for rechargeable lithium-ion batteries used in micromobility devices such as electric bikes and electric scooters. Manufacturers and distributors must comply with specific joint safety standards established by the American National Standards Institute, the Standards Council of Canada, and UL Solutions Inc.

affected_groups.effect: Must comply with specific safety standards for rechargeable lithium-ion batteries used in light electric vehicles, e-bikes, and personal e-mobility devices.
affected_groups.group: Manufacturers and Distributors of Lithium-Ion Batteries and Micromobility Devices

affected_groups.effect: Must issue final product safety rules based on specified standards within 180 days, review future standard revisions, and submit a 5-year hazard report to Congress.

key_provisions: Requires the Consumer Product Safety Commission to promulgate specific existing standards (ANSI/CAN/UL 2271, ANSI/CAN/UL 2849, and ANSI/CAN/UL 2272) as final consumer product safety standards within 180 days of enactment.
Limits the application of the adopted standards to consumer products as defined in the Consumer Product Safety Act.

Establishes a process where future revisions to the voluntary standards automatically become consumer product safety standards after 180 days unless the Commission rejects the revision for failing to improve safety.
Treats any standard promulgated or revised under this act as a consumer product safety rule issued under section 9 of the Consumer Product Safety Act.

Requires the Commission to submit a report to Congress within 5 years detailing fires, explosions, and other hazards related to these lithium-ion batteries, including makes, models, manufacturers, and compliance status if known.

summary_detail.plain_summary: S. 389 requires the Consumer Product Safety Commission to issue a final consumer product safety rule for rechargeable lithium-ion batteries used in micromobility devices such as electric bikes and electric scooters. Manufacturers and distributors must comply with specific joint safety standards established by the American National Standards Institute, the Standards Council of Canada, and UL Solutions Inc.
summary_detail.significance: This bill establishes mandatory federal consumer product safety standards for lithium-ion batteries used in micromobility devices by codifying specific industry standards and setting up a formal mechanism for future updates and congressional reporting on safety hazards.
